note.text:
Chemistry is the study of matter: what substances are made of, their properties, and how they change into new substances.
A chemist asks: What is it made of? How does it behave? What happens when it reacts with something else?
Some branches of chemistry:
• Organic chemistry: compounds of carbon (in living things, fuels, plastics).
• Inorganic chemistry: metals, salts and minerals.
• Physical chemistry: energy changes and how fast reactions go.
• Analytical chemistry: finding what a sample contains.
• Biochemistry: chemical changes inside living things.
A chemist works safely, measures carefully and records results honestly.

worked_example.problem: A laboratory in Douala tests a sample of tap water to find out how much chlorine it contains. Which branch of chemistry is this?
steps: The question is “what does the sample contain, and how much?”
Finding what a sample contains is analytical chemistry.

cards.idea: Chemistry studies matter: what substances are made of, how they behave, and how they change into new substances.
example: When firewood burns, it changes into ash, smoke and gases: new substances. Chemistry studies changes like this.

cards.idea: Chemistry has branches: organic, inorganic, physical, analytical chemistry and biochemistry.
example: Plastics and fuels: organic chemistry. Salts and metals: inorganic chemistry.

cards.idea: A chemist observes, measures carefully, works safely and records results honestly.
example: Ndi weighs a sample twice and writes both results, even when they are different.

right.text: Chemistry studies what substances are made of and how they change.
Burning firewood is a change that chemistry studies.
